record.paper_title: Ductile-to-brittle transition and yielding in soft amorphous materials: perspectives and open questions
record.context_brief: cause or effect of shear bands in brittle yielding
record.original_question: In brittle materials, are shear bands the cause of the abrupt macroscopic stress drop at yielding or an effect of a different failure mechanism, and how should aging, inertia, non-local rheology, finite-size effects, spatial scales, and boundary conditions constrain any theory of heterogeneous yielding flows?

evidence.quote: Yet, in brittle materials, it is still unclear whether shear bands are the cause or the effect of the abrupt stress drop at the yielding transition.
Finally , the impact of aging, possibly combined with inertia, on the yielding scenario, and on heterogeneous flows should also be considered.

Moreover, such a theory should not only provide well-defined qualitative predictions to be checked but also be in quantitative agreement with existing experimental and numerical data. In particular, for ductile yielding, one should account for non-local rheological properties characterized by finite size effects and well-defined spatial scales.

artifact.status_search_result: The question of whether shear bands cause or result from the brittle stress drop at yielding in amorphous solids remains an active open problem. Recent literature (2023–2025) on yielding of amorphous solids, including studies of the ductile-to-brittle transition, random critical points, and spinodal-like scenarios, presents competing pictures but no consensus theory simultaneously incorporating aging, inertia, non-local rheology, finite-size effects, and boundary conditions.

status_evidence.title: Ductile-to-brittle transition and yielding in soft amorphous materials
status_evidence.snippet: Lists open questions on whether shear bands are cause or effect of stress drop, and calls for a theory including aging, inertia, non-local rheology, finite-size, and boundary effects.
status_evidence.claim: The question is explicitly framed as open.

status_evidence.title: Random critical point separates brittle and ductile yielding transitions
status_evidence.snippet: Proposes a random critical point picture for the brittle-ductile yielding transition, but does not resolve the causal role of shear bands or provide a full theory including aging and inertia.
status_evidence.claim: Partial theoretical progress without a complete resolution.
